input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: the wrapper now clears and reuses one statistics dict for every call instead of giving each call its own, so concurrent or nested calls of the same decorated function write into the same dict
- failure path: two threads (or two concurrent awaits of the async wrapper) call the same decorated function; the second call's stats.clear() wipes the first call's start_time and attempt_number, and both read a merged, wrong statistics view afterwards

Reviewer finding
- description: The async wrapper shares one statistics dict across all concurrent invocations and clears it at the start of each call.
- rationale: Trigger: asyncio.gather of several calls to the same decorated coroutine. Each new call clears the shared dict while other calls are mid-retry. Their statistics (attempt_number, idle_for) are reset or mixed, which gives wrong results. Previously each call had an isolated dict.
critique: The finding names the same mechanism: one shared statistics dict that is cleared at the start of each call, so concurrent invocations (asyncio.gather) wipe and mix each other's attempt_number and other stats. That is the same faulty operation and the same failure as the label.
